chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: How McRae came to lead the band after Webb's death
summary: The band played Chicago and New York dates, and when Benny Carter wanted Ella as his own, Moe Gale gave the band to McRae.

bands.name: Ella Fitzgerald and Her Famous Orchestra

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well, what I wanted to do is go back to the tour after Chick's demise -- after you left the Savoy Ballroom.
And you went to Kansas City where you picked up Jessie Price as the drummer who replaced Bill Beeson.
You were on your way to California --
We were on our way to California when we --
Okay. What transpired there? Who was in charge of the band at that time?
I was in charge of the band.
When was the decision made to that actually --
The decision was made --
-- have you be the nominal leader in the band?

-- when we played, I told you we played about four dates out in New York. We were in Pittsburgh. I mean, Pittsburgh was the first big date that we jumped off to after we left the Savoy Ballroom. You know, we went back to the Savoy Ballroom to tune the band up -- to get the band into shape.
After Chick had passed away -- I told you that we went out, we did a couple of theaters and we went out to Chicago. We played the Grand Terrace. We came back --
Earl Hines was there at the same time.

Yeah. Earl Hines was on tour. We played the Grand Terrace while Earl was out. And we stayed there for about four weeks. And we played -- we came back (to (inaudible)) -- We worked our way back into New York and played the Roseland Ballroom. Then we went to the Famous Door right after the Roseland Ballroom. We stayed there for about four weeks. We

broadcast from there.
Now, this was the beginning of the takeover by myself. After we closed the Roseland Ballroom, Moe Gale called a meeting - of the minds, (Inaudible) and members I guess he called Ella (Inaudible) and the band (Inaudible).
He wanted to -- he hired Benny Carter to take over the band. They couldn't come to any agreement with Benny, because Benny said, "It would feature Ella Fitzgerald be Benny Carter's band (Inaudible)." And Moe didn't want that. He wanted Ella to have the band -- Ella Fitzgerald and her band and so and so.
So Benny said, "why don't you give (Inaudible) band to Teddy McRae," you know. (Inaudible).
So he called me in and we made an agreement, so I called rehearsal the next day for the band to report to the Savoy Ballroom.
Well, we opened the Savoy Ballroom for about two weeks. And we stayed there two weeks. In the meanwhile, we got -- still have those dates left.
